title: SVG fundamentals: vector vs raster
learningObjectives: Explain svg fundamentals: vector vs raster and create scalable, accessible graphics or media markup.

understand.concept: SVG is a vector graphics format described using XML-based elements such as paths, shapes, and groups. Raster images store pixels; vector graphics describe geometry and can scale without the same pixelation. SVG can be used as an image file or inline in HTML.
understand.whyItMatters: Vector graphics are useful for icons, diagrams, and scalable illustrations. Complex or untrusted SVG requires careful handling because SVG can contain active features when embedded inline or as a document.
understand.analogy: A raster image is like a mosaic of coloured tiles; a vector image is like a set of drawing instructions that can be rendered at different sizes.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual vector, bitmap, and accessibility behaviour follows the relevant graphics and browser specifications.

explain.narrative: The SVG uses geometric shapes and a path inside a viewBox. It can scale to different display sizes.

examples.code: <svg viewBox='0 0 120 80' role='img' aria-labelledby='title'><title id='title'>Simple vector landscape</title><rect width='120' height='80' fill='#e8f1f8'/><circle cx='88' cy='20' r='10' fill='#e9c46a'/><path d='M0 70 L35 30 L65 70 Z M40 70 L80 25 L120 70 Z' fill='#2a9d8f'/></svg>
examples.explanation: The SVG uses geometric shapes and a path inside a viewBox. It can scale to different display sizes.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered SVG, canvas, or responsive image example.

practise.guidedTask: Compare a small raster icon with an SVG icon at several sizes. Explain when vector graphics are appropriate.
practise.independentTask: Create a small graphic or responsive media example. Include accessible naming or equivalent text and test different display sizes.
hints: Keep important information available as HTML.
Use viewBox for SVG coordinate systems.
Test responsive source selection and image alternatives.

questions.prompt: What is a key difference between vector and raster graphics?
options: Vector graphics describe shapes; raster graphics store pixels
questions.answer: Vector graphics describe shapes; raster graphics store pixels
questions.explanation: SVG describes scalable geometry, while raster formats store pixel data.

questions.prompt: What is a good accessibility practice for meaningful graphics?
options: Provide an accessible name or equivalent information
questions.answer: Provide an accessible name or equivalent information
questions.explanation: Meaningful visual information must also be available through accessible text or equivalent content.
